items.name: Blender MCP + Auto-Rig Pro animation workflow
items.description:
Use this workflow for production animation or rigging work. Blender is 5.0.1. The configured MCP server is `blender-mcp==1.6.4` at loopback `localhost:9876`; its machine install and connection runbook is `/home/kirk/game-dev/docs/blender-mcp-pilot.md`, with configuration in `/home/kirk/game-dev/opencode.json` and installer at `/home/kirk/game-dev/scripts/install-blender-mcp.sh`. Server configuration is not an active GUI connection: enable the Blender add-on and click Connect in every Blender session; never assume a connection persists.

Auto-Rig Pro is local licensed machine state, not bootstrapped or stored in any repository. Before production, inspect Blender Preferences for add-on key `auto_rig_pro-master` (fallback `auto_rig_pro`) and observed version `3.78.34`. Stop and report if it is absent or the version cannot be verified; never silently substitute a different retarget method. Do not provide plugin installation instructions.

MCP is optional for active-GUI inspection and visual iteration only. It has full local control and an exclusive single-client lease, so it is not release truth. Headless repository scripts, tests, and re-import validators, plus Kirk visual approval, are release truth. The canonical retarget recipe's invariants are: use the `BLENDER` glTF import heuristic; derive a dynamic per-target child-joint/rest profile; retain 46 ARP mappings and 47 live constraints while solving; use neither static matrices nor manual production target posing; reach zero final constraints; and validate exact geometry, materials, weights, and action output.
items.example:
Preflight examples (configuration does not prove an active GUI socket):

```sh
jq -e '.mcp["blender-mcp"] | select(.enabled == true and .environment.BLENDER_HOST == "localhost" and .environment.BLENDER_PORT == "9876")' /home/kirk/game-dev/opencode.json
opencode mcp list
# These confirm configured state; neither proves Blender is connected.

blender --background --python-expr 'import bpy, importlib; expected=(3, 78, 34); addons=bpy.context.preferences.addons; key=next((candidate for candidate in ("auto_rig_pro-master", "auto_rig_pro") if candidate in addons), None); assert key, "Auto-Rig Pro is not enabled in Blender Preferences (expected auto_rig_pro-master or auto_rig_pro)"; addon=addons[key]; version=tuple(importlib.import_module(addon.module).bl_info["version"]); print(f"Auto-Rig Pro enabled key={key} version={version}"); assert version == expected, f"Auto-Rig Pro version {version} does not match expected {expected}"'
# Background Blender checks saved Preferences, not an already-open GUI session; verify the enabled add-on and version in Blender Preferences before production.
```

In Blender for every session: enable the Blender MCP add-on, click Connect, then verify Auto-Rig Pro in Preferences before opening the production retarget. Run `rpg-game-assets/scripts/retarget_crypt_idle_walk_arp.py` and `rpg-game-assets/scripts/test_retarget_crypt_idle_walk_arp.py` as the canonical recipe requires; use `rpg-game-assets/.claude/crypt-idle-walk-arp-progress.md` and `game-dev/memory/unarmed-character-animation-workflow.md` for the established sequence. Finish with the repository's headless re-import and exact-output validators, then obtain Kirk visual approval.
items.anti_pattern: Treating `opencode mcp list` or a past Blender session as proof that the GUI socket is connected; treating Auto-Rig Pro as portable or open-source; replacing missing ARP with another retarget method; using MCP-only inspection as release evidence; or shipping retained constraints, static matrices, manual production target poses, or unvalidated output.
